hook: Hold a serious German conversation to the very end: define big ideas, interpret a text, argue with irony and never lose your thread.
intro: The closing conversation of the whole course, in your own AI assistant with voice on: a discussion that moves between an abstract question (freedom, memory, responsibility), a short literary passage to interpret, and a dispute in which the tutor takes the other side. Copy the exercise in, say ‘Los geht’s’, answer in full sentences; the score and corrections come at the end. The tutor listens for six things: an abstract concept named, defined and graded; a literary interpretation that quotes and then interprets; implication and irony in the dispute, marked so they land; modal verbs in their subjective sense to grade certainty and report hearsay (dürfte, müsste, soll, will); long, subordinated turns that keep their thread when the tutor objects; and each turn ending in focus. If you can hold this, you can hold your own in any serious conversation in German.
tips[0].title: Abstract → precise → graded
tips[0].text: Name the concept (Verantwortung, Gewissheit), define it in one sentence (Verantwortung setzt Freiheit voraus), then grade the claim (ist durchaus / keineswegs ausgemacht). Three moves, one strong turn.
tips[0].check.why: keineswegs ausgemacht grades the claim as far from settled; durchaus and gewiss would grade it as certain.
tips[1].title: Interpret with a quotation
tips[1].text: Quote the phrase, then interpret it: Die Wendung „…“ lässt sich als … deuten · verweist auf … · wird gleichsam zu … Never a quotation without its interpretation.
tips[1].check.why: The fixed frame is sich als … deuten lassen; verweisen needs auf, and bedeuten takes no als.
tips[2].title: Dispute with implication and irony
tips[2].text: Say less than you mean, and mark it: Das ist nicht ganz überzeugend (= wrong) · bezeichnenderweise · man könnte meinen … Use one, lightly, and let the argument follow.
tips[2].check.why: bezeichnenderweise says less than it means: it marks the omission as revealing without calling it dishonest outright.
tips[3].title: Modal verbs to grade and to report
tips[3].text: dürfte / müsste (probable), kann nicht (impossible) grade your own certainty; soll (others say) and will (he claims himself) report a claim without endorsing it.
tips[3].check.why: soll passes on what others say without vouching for it; will would mean he claims it himself, dürfte would be your own estimate.
tips[4].title: Hold the thread under objection
tips[4].text: Concede, then return: zugegebenermaßen … im Grunde genommen … nicht zuletzt … Signposts let a long, subordinated turn absorb the counter-argument without losing its line.
tips[4].check.why: zugegebenermaßen concedes the objection first, so that im Grunde genommen can bring the turn back to your line.
tips[5].title: End with focus
tips[5].text: Put the point in the Vorfeld with a particle: Gerade das ist die Frage. Genau darum geht es. Allein das zählt. The last sentence of a turn, focused, is what the listener keeps.
tips[5].check.why: The point stands in the Vorfeld with the focus particle genau, so it is the last thing the listener keeps.
remember[0]: Concept – definition – graded claim; quotation – interpretation.
remember[1]: Implication and irony, lightly and marked; dürfte / soll / will to grade and report.
remember[2]: Signposts hold long turns together; end each turn in focus.
exam: This conversation rehearses C2 exam speaking — and any serious discussion in German where you must defend a view against objections.
